video_title: Which Cavs player could become more important than expected? Wine and Gold Talk podcast

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's mid-season arrival created chemistry challenges for the Cavaliers
quotes.excerpt: James Harden coming to a team in February is difficult. There are a lot of things that have to change.
quotes.quote: The thing that stands out to me, Ethan, is that all of the conversations that so many of the guys were having about this off-season and what it was about from a chemistry-building standpoint, that feels real to me. James Harden coming to a team in February is difficult. There are a lot of things that have to change because of that. Guys talked about maybe not being able to communicate with him the way that they would have liked to because they just didn't know how to communicate to him. Everybody is different, everybody has a different personality. Some leaders lead by example, some lead with their voice, some lead in a more low-key manner. And I think this team was learning James the person, just like they were learning James the basketball player.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's unique playing style required the Cavaliers to adjust their offensive approach
quotes.excerpt: You can't say that we're not going to do any ISO or we're going to play fast.
quotes.quote: You are talking about one of the most unique players of the last 20 years in the NBA who is used to having a system all to himself, who is used to being the man. He had to adjust to the Cavs, the Cavs had to adjust to him. And you get the sense in listening to all these guys at media day that they just didn't have a great grasp of it. Now, it didn't prevent them from getting to the Eastern Conference Finals. That was a big step for this team, but it lets you know that it feels like there is more that you can get from James Harden on the court and there is more that you can get from James Harden off the court. And the only way that you can learn those things is by spending time around each other.

quotes.speaker: Ethan Sands
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Tyson admits to mental lapses and laziness on defense
quotes.excerpt: Jaylen Tyson admitted that there was some simple mental lapses and laziness that he had on the defensive end.
quotes.quote: Jaylen Tyson admitted that there was some simple mental lapses and laziness that he had on the defensive end that prevented him from staying on his assignment and working off-ball, which is pretty hard to do in an off-season, was one of the main points of emphasis for him this off-season. And that's something that we've talked about on this podcast at length that needed to be improved.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Mobley admits to lacking a go-to offensive move
quotes.excerpt: Evan Mobley basically admitted that he had no go-to move whatsoever on the offensive end of the floor.
quotes.quote: Evan Mobley basically admitted that he had no go-to move whatsoever on the offensive end of the floor. And there is no denying that he didn't, and that's part of the reason why, you know, people were wondering, did his game plateau because he was so reliant on his teammates to create for him because he wasn't great at doing that himself? But for him to have that kind of admittance, I thought that was big too.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Jared Allen discusses the emotional impact of the Cavaliers' team identity
quotes.excerpt: Jared Allen had to take a timeout during his press conference to collect his thoughts.
quotes.quote: Jared Allen had to take a timeout during his press conference to collect his thoughts. And it was about how he wanted to describe the legacy, the emotional impact of what this Cleveland Cavaliers organization is trying to do aside from LeBron James, because he even mentioned that Donovan Mitchell doesn't like having the team talk about LeBron because they're trying to separate themselves from that. I thought that was extremely important because we've talked about it on this podcast that this team wants to be different. They want to write their own legacy.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Mario Hezonja's role with the Cavaliers will differ from his time at Real Madrid
quotes.excerpt: What the Cavs are going to ask of him and his role is going to be significantly different.
quotes.quote: I'm inclined to say Mario Hezonja, and I think there are questions. I think there are questions with Hezonja and what the Cavs are going to ask of him and his role is going to be significantly different than the role that he played for Real Madrid. He understands that, he spoke about that. Kenny Atkinson understands that, he has spoken about that. Kobe Altman understands that, he has spoken about that. This is a guy who is getting paid what he's getting paid for a reason because there are legitimate questions about his game and whether it is better equipped for the NBA than what it was early in his career. And he's got to prove that.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Malik Thomas's development and role in the rotation
quotes.excerpt: Malik Thomas has an ability, even as a second-round rookie, to be more involved.
quotes.quote: Let's say this was two years ago and Malik Thomas was coming to the team. There just wasn't an opening for an opportunity as Jaylen Tyson about it. He got 450-plus minutes, barely, as a rookie, and he had to go down to the G League at times to get consistent reps, consistent playing time, and work on his game in meaningful situations, game-like situations. That's not the same roster as two years ago. There are seven yes-definites on this roster. Seven. That's it. So what do you do eight, nine, and 10? Well, yeah, it could be Craig Porter Jr. Sure. It could be Tyrese Proctor. Sure. You can make an argument for all of them, but I don't think there is a separation or a significant separation between Craig Porter Jr., Tyrese Proctor, and Malik Thomas.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Mario Hezonja's physical transformation and defensive potential
quotes.excerpt: He's built like a linebacker. This dude weighs more than Jared Allen.
quotes.quote: Yes, he was a child at the time that he came into the NBA, a child. And now he's coming back as a man, a seasoned man who has played against some of the highest-level competition outside the NBA overseas. And now he's 6'9" and 260 pounds. As you mentioned, that's heavier than Jared Allen. It's more stocky. We've heard different guys talk about how you're not going to be able to move him off his spot, but he's also going to be able to wall up against some of these bigger guys as well.

quotes.speaker: Chris Fedor
quotes.summary_phrase: Peyton Watson's addition saved the Cavaliers' off-season
quotes.excerpt: I think Peyton Watson saved the off-season. And again, you don't want to go overboard.
quotes.quote: I think Peyton Watson saved the off-season. And again, you don't want to go overboard and I don't want to be hyperbolic here, because I think even coming off of a sweep against the Knicks where the Cavs just weren't competitive in the final three games, the organization itself was in a good place. Okay, and this was a good basketball team. It was not a bad basketball team. But at one point throughout the course of this off-season, the other teams were starting to distance themselves from the Cavs. They were starting to pull away a little bit in the Eastern Conference arms race. I think Peyton Watson saved the off-season.
